draft.solen_current: LOCKFILE.md §11 (Imagery Pattern Registry, V3-D330, lines 1122 to 1180) already codifies: 5 enumerated layout patterns (split-hero, full-bleed editorial, search-card-over-photo, alternating rows, magazine grid), 5 non-negotiable rules (border-radius 0 with named exceptions, no flat rgba overlay wash with the DS-10 gradient-scrim carve-out, no video except the Entdecken TikTok-stream exemption, single next/image + Supabase Storage CDN pipeline, same image mobile+desktop), a text-on-photo scrim recipe (DS-10), a sourcing policy (AI placeholders during sweep, lazy real-photo swap), a migration mapping table for the phase-2 sweep, and a canonical aspect-ratio set (1:1, 3:2, 16:9, 21:9, 4:3) enforced by drift rule A11. PSYCHOLOGY.md law 7 (line 34) already owns the commercial/behavioral case for photos as decision input, not decoration, with two sourced stats. PHOTO_STRATEGY.md is a narrow spike covering only the 6 category-landing heroes: CDN choice (no new vendor, Netlify+next/image), AI placeholder source (Nano Banana), a manual owner quality gate, and a generation spec (3:2 master, subject right-weighted, Swiss-plausible interiors, no readable faces). None of these three documents state a site-wide imagery density/ratio floor (what fraction of a page or card grid should be photographic versus text/chrome, beyond the 6 heroes), nor a general PDP/card photo treatment rule beyond the existing §11 patterns, nor art-direction rules (lighting, composition, cropping discipline) for imagery outside the category-hero spike.
draft.gap: The gap named in the stream (a site-wide imagery density/ratio floor, general PDP/card photo treatment, and art-direction rules beyond the 6 category heroes PHOTO_STRATEGY.md covers) is real: LOCKFILE §11 governs WHAT PATTERN to use and HOW to render an image once one exists, but not HOW MUCH imagery a given surface should carry or WHERE the floor sits. PHOTO_STRATEGY.md only resolves this for the 6 static category heroes, not for dynamic salon/search/dashboard surfaces generally. However, the stream's own key_question is explicit: "BLOCKED pending a fresh owner yes... Do not research until the owner re-opens G6." Producing a full generative prior (numeric imagery-share bands, per-surface photo treatment rules, art-direction guidelines) here would violate that instruction and would front-run an owner decision that has not been made. This report therefore stops at naming the gap and does not attempt to close it.
draft.proposed_addition:
PARKING NOTE ONLY (no prior drafted, per gating instruction):

What an owner "yes" on G6 would unlock: a computable, site-wide imagery-density prior (analogous to S01's richness/restraint prior, gap_ref G1) that would tell a first mockup how much photographic content a given surface class needs (search results grid, PDP body beyond the hero, dashboard, category landings beyond the 6 already speced) before it reads as either "photo-starved and monochrome" or "cluttered." It would also extend LOCKFILE §11's 5 patterns with general art-direction rules (lighting consistency, subject framing, crop discipline for user-uploaded salon photos versus AI-placeholder or licensed-stock photos) that today exist only for the 6 static category heroes in PHOTO_STRATEGY.md.

Why it stays parked: the stream's key_question is marked BLOCKED with an explicit "do not research until the owner re-opens G6" instruction. The commercial/behavioral case for imagery (photos as decision input, not decoration) is already settled and lives in PSYCHOLOGY.md law 7; what remains gated is the DESIGN-SYSTEM commitment (a numeric floor, a build obligation across surfaces beyond the 6 heroes) which carries real cost (photography, AI-generation, or licensing spend) that only the owner can authorize. Re-opening G6 is therefore a scope-and-budget decision, not a research gap. When the owner reopens it, the correct next step is to run this stream's research proper: source a T1/T2 imagery-density study if one exists (none was found or asserted here), then draft a generative prior in the shape the stream calls for (numeric bands: imagery share, per-surface treatment, art-direction rules) plus a short Taste-Lab probe comparing 2 to 3 density variants on a real Solen surface (e.g. search results) to calibrate the floor empirically rather than by assertion.

Not a myth-table entry, not inflated.

verified.residual_risks: No claim failed verification and no myth-table number was cited, so this stream needed no correction, only tier confirmation. One residual gap worth flagging to the owner as a QUESTIONS.md candidate (not a lock change): both sourced studies (Airbnb occupancy, Baymard first-look) establish that photo PRESENCE and quality matter, but neither speaks to imagery DENSITY or RATIO (what fraction of a page/grid should be photographic). If G6 is reopened, the research stage will need a fresh density-specific source or will have to fall back to a Taste-Lab probe as the primary evidence rather than a cited study, since no located source currently answers the actual G6 question. This does not weaken the parking note itself, which correctly stops short of inventing a density number.
